title: Adaptive tail-trimmer & kernel-swapper for mixed prefill/stream workloads
creator: Avery Kim
description:
Background: Our serving runtime spends significant GPU cycles on padded tokens when handling heterogeneous request lengths, particularly for mixed prefill + streaming decode workloads. Existing bucketing reduces worst-case padding but leaves headroom: (1) many requests have short remaining decode horizon but are padded to a longer bucket because prefill lengths vary, and (2) kernel selection is static per-model or per-batch and does not react to dynamic sequence-length composition.

Goal: Implement an adaptive micro-batch shaping feature that combines (A) tail-trimming to opportunistically remove trailing padding at pack time, (B) per-batch kernel swapping based on observed effective sequence lengths and attention pattern, and (C) a prefill-aware scheduling policy that co-schedules short-decode-prefill-heavy requests with long-prefill-short-decode ones to reduce net padding. The objective is to reduce average padded tokens, lower p95 decode latency, and reduce GPU token-cost by at least 8-12% on mixed workloads without regressing p50 latency or model quality.

Design summary:
- Prediction and tagging: On request enqueue, compute a cheap remaining-horizon heuristic: remaining_tokens = max(user_header_hint, sequence_end_token_prediction(history_embedding_length)). Tag requests with predicted remainder buckets (short/medium/long).
- Tail-trimmer: At pack time, evaluate the batch skyline and detect trailing columns that are fully padding or that will be produced after a high-confidence EOS prediction window. Remove those columns from the micro-batch GPU tensor and attach metadata mapping for per-request runtime reassembly. This is safe only when the model or heuristic indicates EOS within a tolerant threshold; otherwise fall back to conservative packing.
- Kernel-swapper: Maintain two kernel profiles per architecture: low-latency short-seq kernels (fused attention kernels optimized for short KV sizes) and throughput-preferring kernels (block-sparse/quantized paths). At batch dispatch, choose kernel profile according to the effective max-seqlen after tail-trim and the attention pattern flag. Provide a lightweight cost model to estimate per-kernel tokens/sec for current batch composition.
- Prefill-aware scheduler: Distinguish prefill vs decode segments in incoming requests. When packing, prefer pairing long-prefill-short-decode requests with short-prefill-long-decode requests so prefill alignment reduces total padding. The scheduler greedily builds micro-batches with a mixed composition target ratio configurable per deployment.
- Safety and fallbacks: If any request in a micro-batch has unknown EOS confidence or uses unsupported ops, disable tail-trim for that batch. Expose a per-customer flag to opt-out for deterministic padding when required by downstream tooling.

Metrics and targets:
- Primary metrics: padded_tokens_per_1000 = tokens_padded / tokens_generated * 1000; GPU_token_seconds; p50/p95 decode latency; successful_tail_trims_percent; model_quality_delta (ROUGE/BLEU or embedding drift).
- Targets: padded_tokens_per_1000 down 10% (baseline mixed workload), p95 decode latency down 15-20%, GPU token-cost down 8-12%, model_quality_delta <= 0.5% for evaluated prompt set.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype tail-trim logic in the local micro-batcher simulator and unit tests (2 wks).
2) Implement kernel cost-model and kernel selection hooks in runtime scheduler (3 wks).
3) Add prefill-aware greedy packer and config flags (2 wks).
4) Integration tests against internal benchmark harness (1 week).
5) Canary rollout to dedicated pool, monitor metrics & rollback gate (2 weeks).

Trade-offs and risks:
- Risk: Wrong EOS heuristics could incorrectly trim tokens and alter outputs. Mitigation: conservative confidence threshold, shadow mode with verification, and customer opt-out.
- Risk: Kernel switching overhead could negate gains for borderline batches. Mitigation: include kernel swap cost in cost model and enforce minimum batch duration for swap to be beneficial.
- Observability: Requires per-token mapping telemetry to verify reassembly correctness; add lightweight checksum checks in early canary.

Rollout & flags:
- Feature flags: runtime.tail_trim.enabled, runtime.kernel_swap.threshold_ms, runtime.prefill_mixer.ratio. Default: off in hosted API, opt-in for Dedicated; enable in Private with admin toggle.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation: micro-batcher simulator shows >=8% reduction in padded tokens on mixed workload traces
Unit tests and integration tests validate no decoding divergence for approved prompt suite
Canary in dedicated pool achieves target padded token reduction and p95 decode latency improvement without quality regression
Observability: dashboard with per-batch trimmed columns, kernel profile chosen, and checksum pass rates
Docs: runtime/README and console feature toggle entries updated
comments: 2026-01-29 Marcus Stone: Spike completed for tail-trim heuristics using EOS-confidence from small probe head. Simulator shows early promise (simulated padded tokens -12% on sampled traces). Next: add conservative reassembly map and checksum validation.

2026-02-06 Avery Kim: Design sync notes uploaded to Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1rX-TAILTRIM-DOC (internal). Key decision: prefer conservative trimming threshold (0.95 EOS confidence) for canary to minimize risk.

2026-02-18 Marcus Stone: Kernel cost model v0 merged to runtime on branch feature/kernel-swapper. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2893. Benchmarks: short-kernel wins for effective seqlen <= 64 with 1.2x latency reduction in synthetic tests.

2026-02-25 QA: Integration harness run id=bench-20260225 shows padded_tokens_per_1000 -9.7%, p95 decode -16% on mixed traffic replay. One regression case found for a long-context multi-turn convo; added to exclusion list (low-confidence EOS).
2026-03-03 Security review: no PII exfil risk identified. We store only mapping metadata and transient checksums during canary. Security note: KMS unchanged.
